summary: Phase 6 (early start): write the docs/ tree — concept pages, per-experiment pages with migrated lab notes, device page, hardware, bring-up workflow, troubleshooting, glossary

open_questions: Trigger pin 0 (PMOD): nothing in the code says what it drives (an RF switch on the drive line, a scope trigger, or nothing). Rabi, T1, T2E and single shot fire it. Spec, chi shift, T2R, T1_SS, the charge-dispersion steps, ModifiedRamsey, ActiveResetVerify, UndrivenSingleShot and ZeroSpanParity do not. If it gates the drive, those steps play their pulses into a closed switch. Please confirm the wiring.

Most regime-A programs (CavitySpecFF, QubitSpecSliceFF, both Rabi classes, ChiShift, T1FF, T2EMUX, T2R, ChargeDispersion, QuasiCW, T1_SS), plus ZeroSpanParity, call declare_readout(length=us2cycles(readout_length)) without ro_ch. In qick 0.2.334 that length counts readout samples, so on this board the window comes out 1.4x the requested length: for a 15 us request it runs to about 21.3 us while the tone stops at 15.3 us. I worked this out from the clock values; it has not been measured. Has anyone seen this on hardware? Should it go on the fix list? It is documented as a Known issue in concepts/readout_window.md.
How were the ADC offsets chosen: 0.3 us for the regime-A and single-shot windows, 0.488 us for zero-span? Nothing records the reason (line latency, ring-up, a scan).
Board qick version: shot_buffers.py says 'the BFG board runs 0.2.367'. Is the BFG board the same board as myqick at 192.168.0.103?

DAC sampling rate (gens[ch]['fs']) for res_ch and qubit_ch on the current board, and whether readout near 7.29 GHz with nqz=2 and qubit up to about 3.75 GHz with qubit_nqz=1 are the intended zones. I gave no numbers, only told readers to check soccfg.

When run() switches from regime B back to A, does it rebuild from scratch (earlier A carry-overs lost) or restore a cached A config, as interleave does? Design v3 does not say. The docs assume the carry-overs are lost.

Two pages name the single-shot T1 step differently. experiments/README.md and running_a_session.md use 't1_ss'; experiments/t1_single_shot.md uses 't1_single_shot' / R.t1_single_shot(). I used t1_ss. One name needs picking and the pages aligning.
What does BFC stand for? CLAUDE.md says Broadband Flux Control, the code never spells it out, and the glossary leaves it unexpanded.
The old cavity winding calibration (0.45917414 / 1.0903695; -32.10723885+pi / -15.77597) has no device or date. Keep it on iq_conventions.md as 'historical, not in use', or drop it?
The 2026-06-02 'Q6 QubitSpecFF' projection example does not name its device. Is it CSTQ03?
Kappa of the CSTQ03 resonators has not been measured. The guide reset_readout_relax_delay >= 6/kappa currently rests on the TATQ01/BFE Q2 value (190 kHz, 2026-06-06).

README.md links quickstart.md and parameters.md, which do not exist yet. troubleshooting.md links experiments/zero_span_parity.md, which another agent has not written yet. All other links and anchors in my nine pages were checked and resolve.

Per-qubit readout windows: the runner notes give 5 us for CSTQ03 Q2 and 'Q1 15 us, Q5 5 us' for single shot, but the device defaults are 15 us / 0.3 us. Should Q2 and Q5 carry their own Readout.window / ss_window in devices/CSTQ03.py?

Why must T2E num_pi_pulses be odd? The runner and AUTO_COHERENCE_PARAMS state the rule, but nothing in the code records the reason. With pi/2 at 0 deg and pi at 90 deg (CPMG), an even n should also refocus. t2_echo.md says the reason is unknown and calls even values untested.

What does PMOD pin 0 drive on the current setup (a switch gating the drive path, a scope trigger, ...)? Rabi, T1, T2E and SingleShot fire it; two_tone_spec, chi_shift and T2R do not. If it gates the drive, the chi_shift pi pulse is blocked. The pages say this is undocumented and point to hardware.md.

Step name for T1_SS: running_a_session.md calls the step `t1_ss`, but the sibling page is t1_single_shot.md and uses `R.t1_single_shot()`. The README index uses t1_ss and links to t1_single_shot.md; one name needs to be chosen.
Step names for the cw_tones page: I used `constant_two_tone` and `constant_tone`, which match running_a_session.md. Please confirm.

trans_qubit_spec: what was 'Trans' meant to mean? The code only repeats two_tone_spec at base-config settings `repetitions` times. No transmission is measured, relax_delay falls back to BASE_CONFIG's 3000 us, and the repetition count is borrowed from T1T2_params. Is this the intended behaviour?
auto_coherence reads drive frequency, gain, sigma and flat-top from Qubit_Parameters[qubit_readout] and ignores qubit_pulse. Is that intended? It matters only when the two differ.

Two CSTQ03 runner comments are ambiguous: "500 used for charge sweeps" in Spec_relevant_params (spec gain or relax_delay?), and "qubit_length 10 was best for Q4" (which device and date?). Both are recorded on the pages as not recorded / ambiguous.
Lab note 'Q6 2026-06-02 QubitSpecFF' (feature at ~3054 MHz missed): which device was this? The docstring gives only the qubit and date. It is attributed on two_tone_spec.md as 'device not recorded'.
Hanger kappa: should the reported kappa be the total linewidth f0/Qtot (in MHz, without the /1e6)? Today it is (f0/Qext)/1e6. The page tells users to compute f0/Qtot from hanger_fit_popt.
constant_tone (SingleTone) calls acquire() on a program with no declared readout. Has this ever been run on hardware, and does it return or hang?

README.md links ../parameters.md, which does not exist yet (it is meant to be generated in phase 6). Five index rows are marked '(pending)' because their pages do not exist yet: two_tone_charge_dispersion_quasicw, charge_dispersion_quasicw, charge_dispersion_ramsey, charge_sweep, charge_transmission_sweep and zero_span_parity. They need links once those pages are written.

Recipe keyword spellings in the PLAN snippets are provisional, e.g. R.two_tone_spec(gain=..., spec_span=..., spec_num_points=...), R.chi_shift(cavity_shift=..., trans_span=...), R.interleaved_coherence(cycles=..., t2e=...), and the legacy-cased keys in R.auto_coherence(T1_step=...). They should be reconciled with qicklab/runs/recipes.py when it is written.
The cd_max 0.682 MHz / cd_period 4.37 mV calibration has no device, qubit or date recorded. It is cited on auto_coherence.md as the value for Strategy A.

Which modified_ramsey relax setting is meant? The CSTQ03 runner has mr_relax_delay=500 and mr_reps=50000, commented '5x T1=50us' (that is 250 us). Your 2026-08-04 acceptance settings were 250 us and 100000 shots, marked 'KEEP'.

Are the 2026-10-01 cooldown modified_ramsey values measured: f_ge=3754.5, df=1, tau_harmonic_k=1? 3754.5 MHz is Q2's centre frequency, but the session pulse qubit is Q5, and the adjacent comment says 'measured TOP branch (bottom = 4184.0)'.

Is the CSTQ03 Q2 doublet 4186.7/4184.0 MHz (df = 2.7 MHz, measured 2026-08-04) really charge parity? It is 4x cd_max_mhz = 0.682. Which device and date does the charge-dispersion model (cd_max 0.682 MHz, period 4.37 mV) come from?
Is the cd_period_mv the period of S(V) or of the cosine inside it? With S(V)=cd_max|cos(2pi(V-V0)/T)| as written, the Strategy-A jump of T/2 lands at the same separation.
Has kappa been measured for the CSTQ03 readout resonator? reset_readout_relax_delay = 5 us is 6/kappa for TATQ01/BFE Q2 (kappa/2pi = 190 kHz, 2026-06-06).
Should the active-reset read-latency stall fix (Alex Place, commit 4be2b7a on bfg_code) be ported? It is not in this tree, so active_reset.md and active_reset_verify.md list it as a known issue.

Some facts come only from your session memory, not from code or audits: the 250 us acceptance-run r(1) values, the randomised tau-sweep null, the TATQ01-SiO2 Q3 read-latency evidence, and the 0.74/0.78 reset ceiling. They are labelled 'lab record'. Confirm they may be published, or say which to drop.
Which device and date does the charge-dispersion doublet 2306.310396 / 2306.567327 / 2306.032673 MHz belong to? And is ChargeDispersion's 1/df wait intended? The phase argument gives 1/(2df).
What do these runner notes mean: 'voltage_step ... 0.0001 has two periods in it', and is '500 used for charge sweeps' a gain or a relax delay?
What does trigger pin 0 drive on the current setup? SingleShot, Rabi, T1 and T2E fire it.

TWPA bias: does '18 (10/7/26)' mean 18 uA set on 2026-10-07? That is above the ~11 uA datasheet guidance. What is the current operating point? The committed target is 0 and DISABLE_PUMP=True is committed.
The ZeroSpanParity decimated defaults (read_length 80 us) fail rule 5 at buf_maxlen 1024. What values are intended for Path B?
modified_ramsey_control accepts a sweet spot at sep < 0.1 MHz, but the peak finder never returns two peaks closer than 0.10 MHz. Is acceptance meant to come only from a single peak?
Are the single-shot readout times still valid for CSTQ03 ('Q1 15 us, Q5 5 us; keep at 15')?

The experiments_a index (docs/experiments/README.md, another group's file, not edited) lists my pages as '(pending)' and names the T1_SS step 't1_ss'. My page uses t1_single_shot.md and covers charge_dispersion_quasicw, charge_dispersion_ramsey and two_tone_charge_dispersion_quasicw in one charge_dispersion.md. The index needs reconciling.

Step names: the experiments index (another group) lists 't1_ss' but a page experiments/t1_single_shot.md also exists. I used t1_ss, t2_ramsey, t2_echo and interleaved_coherence. Pick one name per step before the STEPS registry lands.

Design ambiguity: R.single_shot() appears both as a Session group (single_shot=R.single_shot()) and as a PLAN step. Should one recipe return both a group and a Step, or should the group get its own name? The same question applies to how run_step handles regime switches, and where dry_run writes its files (if anywhere).
The design layout says runners/session.py; the task and the critique say runners/<device>_session.py. The docs use runners/CSTQ03_session.py.

CSTQ03 'currently working on N' comments per slot (current Q1->2, Q2->4, Q3->3, Q4->5, Q5->'6?'; v2b Q1->3, Q2->6, Q3->4, Q5->5, Q6->2): what do they mean (physical label, readout line, something else)?

Is the 'v2b nu cell' table a previous cooldown of CSTQ03 or a sibling chip? The 2026-08-04 Modified Ramsey doublet midpoint (4185.35 MHz) matches v2b Q2 (4185.6), not current Q2 (3754.5), so it was probably measured under the v2b set. Please confirm.
Reconcile df = 2.7 MHz (CSTQ03 Q2, 2026-08-04) with cd_max_mhz = 0.682 MHz / cd_period_mv = 4.37 mV. Which qubit, cooldown and date does that charge-dispersion calibration belong to?
Identity (device, qubit, date) of the charge-dispersion doublet 2306.310396 / 2306.567327 / 2306.032673 MHz.

What do these undated runner notes mean: charge_params '0.0001 has two periods in it', and '500 used for charge sweeps' (relax_delay or gain)? Which qubit is 'start_voltage 0.0059 V working for good T2Rs' for, and which device is 'qubit_length 10 was the best for Q4' for?

Modified Ramsey: is mr_relax_delay meant to be 500 us or the recommended 250 us (5 x T1)? Is mr_reps meant to be 50k or the recommended 100k? The runner also still has df=1, tau_harmonic_k=1 and f_ge=3754.5 (stale).
Readout kappa has not been measured for CSTQ03, and reset_readout_relax_delay = 5 us is based on TATQ01/BFE. Who measures it, and for which resonators?
TWPA bias for the 2026-10-01 cooldown: the committed target is 0 uA with the note '18 (10/7/26)'. Is 18 uA (set 2026-10-07?) the operating point? It is above the datasheet's ~11 uA guidance.
What does tProc trigger pin 0 drive in the current wiring (switch, scope, ...)?
Should Q2 and Q5 get per-qubit 5 us readout / single-shot windows? Notes say Q2 'readout length 5 us' and SS 'Q5 5 us', but also 'keep at 15'.
Q1 and Q3 pi/2 gain is 3975//2 while their pi gain is 5000. Is that intentional or carried over from another qubit?
Keep the 4-entry FF_Qubits map (persisted but never read) as Setup.ff_qubits for CSTQ03, or drop it?
The board qick version 0.2.367 comes only from the shot_buffers docstring. Please confirm against the board.

remaining: docs/quickstart.md does not exist. Item 1 of the README reading path now points to running_a_session.md#the-session-file and #running until someone writes the page. Write it or drop the item.

docs/parameters.md does not exist yet (it is generated in phase 6 by scripts/gen_docs.py, which is not written). I removed all 5 links to it (README, running_a_session, experiments/README, undriven_single_shot, charge_transmission_sweep) and left plain-text forward references. Restore the links once the generator exists.

Code comment is wrong (outside docs/, not edited): mModifiedRamsey.py around line 609 says the fixed 2^24 offset fails 'beyond ~0.5 us'. From its own bound (|raw I| <= ro_norm*2^15) the crossover is 512 readout cycles, about 1.7 us at f_output 307.2 MHz, which matches the '9x too small at 15 us' figure. I corrected architecture.md, active_reset.md and iq_conventions.md (2 places); the code comment needs fixing in the refactor.

Physics constant to decide: the Modified Ramsey planner and program use rabi_pi2_mhz = 0.0997/sigma. That is the untruncated-Gaussian value; QICK's 4-sigma envelope (cut at +/-2 sigma, no offset subtraction) gives about 0.1045/sigma, so the code overstates the bandwidth ratio by about 5% (the conservative direction). I added a note to modified_ramsey.md and kept the code-derived CSTQ03 numbers (1.354, 2.708, 0.0739, 0.0369 us). Changing the constant would change program behaviour, so it needs a separate fix commit and a golden update.

Device attribution unknown: the utils.py note on the 2026-06-02 Q6 QubitSpecFF spectroscopy (feature at 3054 MHz, noise spikes at 3038/3069 MHz) does not name the device. devices/CSTQ03.md and bringup_workflow.md had stated it as CSTQ03; they now say 'device not recorded'. Confirm which chip it was.

Legacy paths left on purpose: running_a_session.md line 9 status note names Runners/CSTQ03_BFC.py as the current working runner (correct for this branch until phase 5), and architecture.md line 98 says 'legacy CoreLib comment' as attribution for the Ge Yang quote. No mT*.py or Runners/runs/... paths were found anywhere in docs/.

Open device questions already listed under 'Open items' in devices/CSTQ03.md: meaning of 'currently working on N'; df 2.7 MHz (2026-08-04) vs cd_max_mhz 0.682 MHz; kappa never measured for CSTQ03; mr_relax_delay 250 vs 500 us and mr_reps 50k vs 100k; whether Q2 and Q5 get per-qubit 5 us readout windows; identity of the 2306.3 MHz doublet; TWPA bias 18 uA (2026-10-07 note) vs the committed 0.

modified_ramsey_control Strategy A jumps half a period, but the documented model S(V)=cd_max*|cos(2pi(V-V0)/T)| repeats every T/2, so the jump lands where S is unchanged. It is documented as a known issue; decide whether the model or the jump is intended.
BFC acronym: glossary.md says the code never spells it out, while CLAUDE.md expands it as 'Broadband Flux Control'. Confirm and add it to the glossary if correct.

Every page describes the phase-5 API (Session, R.<step> recipes, run, Device dataclasses, record_calibration, core.readout, core.active_reset, core.fakes), and none of it exists on the branch yet. Recipe keyword spellings in the snippets are illustrative and need checking against recipes.py once it lands.
